## At A Glance

| Item | Quiz 3 arrangement |
|---|---|
| When | **Week 10, not Week 9**; exact date and meeting for each section in Blackboard |
| Coverage | **R only, Weeks 6–9 inclusive**; no MATLAB or Week 10 material |
| Preparation focus | R foundations, transformations, exploratory analysis, import and tidy data from Weeks 6–9 |
| Proposed format | 15 minutes; 9 single-choice questions and 3 short written responses; 12 points |
| Delivery | In-class Blackboard quiz; final settings and permitted materials will be confirmed in Blackboard |

The schedule and **R-only coverage of Weeks 6–9 inclusive** are confirmed.
MATLAB is not included. The detailed format awaits final instructor confirmation.
The preparation below and practice activity follow this confirmed scope.

## What To Practise

| Week | Core skills |
|---|---|
| [6](../weeks/week-06.qmd) | R vectors and missing values; recorded zero versus `NA`; saved scripts, clean runs and consistent rendered reports |
| [7](../weeks/week-07.qmd) | Read short pipelines; distinguish rows from columns; filtering, grouping and summaries; retain observed denominators; match a pipeline to its question |
| [8](../weeks/week-08.qmd) | Choose plots for variable types; interpret distributions and comparisons; bin width and overplotting; investigate anomalies; distinguish association from causation |
| [9](../weeks/week-09.qmd) | Relative paths, import schemas, missing encodings and parsing diagnostics; wide-to-long reshaping; row meaning, expected row counts and observation keys |

You should be able to read a short piece of R code or a small result and state
what it does, which observations contribute, and what check or limitation
matters. You do not need to write a long program from a blank page. Practice
simple calculations by hand; the proposed quiz does not require running R.

Week 10 joins, string normalization, factor conversion and date-time parsing
are **not included**. Modeling first introduced later in the course is not
included either. The core exercises are the preparation priority; extension
tasks are not assumed knowledge for this quiz.

## Practice And Revision

1. Review the survival checklists and core exercises for Weeks 6–9.
2. Trace a small pipeline by hand, recording row counts and row meaning.
3. Distinguish original row count from the number of observed values entering
   a mean. Missing values are not automatically zeros.
4. For each plot, state a supported observation and one limitation.
5. Predict a reshape's size and explain why row count alone cannot validate it.
6. Attempt the [separate practice quiz](quiz-03-practice.qmd), then open its
   self-check feedback. Its situations differ from the live versions.

For short written answers, answer the requested parts directly. Equivalent
correct wording is accepted; polished English and extra unrequested details
are not needed. The proposed written rubric uses two explicit half-point
criteria per question, and the MCQs have one best answer each.

## Proposed Materials And Delivery Rules

The prepared versions follow Quiz 2's arrangement: one A4 sheet handwritten by
the student on both sides, blank scratch paper, individual work, and no R,
AI, websites, messaging or collaboration. There is no need for a calculator.
Final rules, timing, accommodations and the access window will be confirmed in
Blackboard before the quiz. A paper backup is available to the instructor.

The [syllabus missed-assessment policy](../syllabus/index.qmd#missed-assessments-and-late-project-submissions)
continues to apply. Live quiz questions and their answer keys are not published
on this website.
